farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ﴾: on the day of Badr the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the people, saying: "شاهت الوجوه" ("May the faces be disfigured"), that is, may they be made ugly; and that too was a cause of their rout.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾, and also (موَهِّن). If you wish you put it in iḍāfa (genitive construct), and if you wish you give it tanwīn (nunation) and put [the following noun] in the accusative. Like it are (إنّ اللّهَ بَالِغُ أمْرِهِ، وبَالغٌ أمْرَهُ) and (كاشفاتُ ضُرِّه، وكاشِفَاتٌ ضُرَّه).

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾: Abū Jahl said on that day: "O Allah, give victory to the better of the two religions and the one more deserving of victory." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾, meaning victory.
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: he said: putting a kasra on its alif (i.e. reading إِنَّ) is dearer to me than putting a fatḥa on it, because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (وإن الله لمع المؤمنين), and this makes the kasra good, as the beginning of a new sentence. Whoever gives it a fatḥa connects it with ﴿وَلَن تُغْنِيَ عَنْكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ﴾, meaning: "because of its great number and because Allah is with the believers"; so its position is accusative (naṣb), since the genitive (khafḍ) [i.e. an implied preposition] is suitable in it.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتْنَةً لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ﴾: He commanded them and then forbade them, and there is in it a touch of the jazāʾ (conditional apodosis), even though it is a prohibition. Like it is His saying ﴿يأيها النمل ادخلوا مساكِنكم لا يحطِمنَّكم﴾: she commanded them and then forbade them, and there is in it the sense of the jazāʾ.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُوۤاْ إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ﴾ was revealed about the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn) specifically.
His saying: ﴿فَآوَاكُمْ﴾ means: to Medina; ﴿وَأَيَّدَكُم بِنَصْرِهِ﴾ means: He strengthened you.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَخُونُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ وَتَخُونُوۤاْ أَمَانَاتِكُمْ﴾: if you wish you make it jussive (jazm) as a prohibition, and if you wish you make it ṣarf (the "turning-away" construction) and put it in the accusative. [The poet] said:
لا تنه عن خُلُقٍ وتأتِىَ مِثلَه * عار عليك إِذا فعلت عظيم
(Do not forbid a trait while you yourself do its like; a great shame upon you if you do.)
And in one of the two readings it is (ولا تخونوا أماناتِكم), so here too it may be jussive or accusative.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿إَن تَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّكُمْ فُرْقَاناً﴾: He says: an opening (victory) and help. Likewise His saying ﴿يوم الفرقانِ يوم التقى الجمعانِ﴾: the day of the opening and of victory.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾: a group of Quraysh gathered and said: "What is your view about Muḥammad ﷺ?" Iblīs came in among them in the form of a man from the people of Najd. ʿAmr ibn Hishām said: "My view is that you confine him in a house, plaster it up over him, open a small window for him and press hard on him until he dies." Iblīs rejected that and said: "What a bad opinion your opinion is!" Abū al-Bakhtarī ibn Hishām said: "My view is that he be put on a camel and then driven off with it until he perishes, or some of the Arabs rid you of him." Iblīs said: "What a bad opinion! Would you send away from yourselves a man who has corrupted most of you, so that he falls in with others than you? Perhaps he would then raid you with them." The wicked one, Abū Jahl, said: "My view is that we go to him with a man from every clan of Quraysh and strike him with our swords." Iblīs said: "The right opinion is what this young man has given." Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ with the news, and he left Mecca, he and Abū Bakr. So His saying (ليثبتوك) means: to confine you in the house; (أو يخرِجوك): on the camel; (أو يقتلوك).
[Translator's note: the source writes «صى الله عليه وسلم», evidently a misprint for «صلى الله عليه وسلم»; rendered as ﷺ.]

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ ٱللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَـٰذَا هُوَ ٱلْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ﴾: in (الحق) there is the accusative and the nominative. If you make (هو) a noun [i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject)], you put الحق in the nominative by هو. If you make it an ʿimād (support pronoun; the Kufan term for the separating pronoun), functioning like a ṣila (redundant link), you put الحق in the accusative. Do the same with the sisters of kāna, and with aẓunnu (I think) and its sisters, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿ويرى الذِين أوتو العِلم الذى أنزِل إليك مِن ربك هو الحق﴾: you put الحق in the accusative because (رأيت) is one of the sisters of ẓanantu. Every place where yafʿalu or faʿala would be suitable in place of the accusative "fiʿl" [i.e. the predicate] admits the ʿimād and the accusative of that "fiʿl"; and it also admits its nominative by هو, if you make it a noun. And the alif and lām (the definite article) are indispensable when you find a way to them. So if you say: وجدت عبدالله هو خيرا منك وشرا منك أو أفضل منك ("I found ʿAbd Allāh better than you / worse than you / more excellent than you"), then in whatever resembles this "fiʿl" there is both accusative and nominative: the accusative on the basis that the alif and lām are intended, even if they cannot be inserted; and the nominative on the basis that you make (هو) a noun. So you say: ظننت أخاك هو أصغُر منك and هو أصغرَ منك ("I thought your brother younger than you").
When you come to proper nouns such as ʿAmr and Muḥammad, or to nouns in iḍāfa such as أبيك (your father) and أخيك (your brother), you put them in the nominative, saying: أظنّ زيدا هو أخوك and أظنّ أخاك هو زيد, putting it in the nominative, since you have not brought the sign of the "returned" element (al-mardūd) but have brought هو, which is the sign of the noun. The sign of the "returned" element is that every "fiʿl" which has no alif and lām is brought back with alif and lām and refers back to the noun; so (هو) is a support for the noun and (the alif and lām) a support for the "fiʿl". Since the alif and lām could not be supplied, and it was not proper to intend them in زيد, because it is a [proper] name, nor in الأخ, because it is in iḍāfa, they preferred the nominative. It is proper in (أفضل منك) because you drop (من) and say: رأيتك أنت الأفضل ("I saw you to be the most excellent"); but it is not proper in (زيد) or in (الأخ) to intend an alif and lām. Al-Kisāʾī used to allow it, saying: رأيت أخاك هو زيدا and رأيت زيدا هو أخاك. And it is permissible, just as it was permissible in (أفضل) because of the intention, the intention of the alif and lām; and likewise it was permissible in زيد and أخيك. When the alif and lām are possible for you and yet you do not bring them, use the nominative; so you say: رأيت زيدا هو قائم and رأيت عمرا هو جالس.
The poet said:
إجِدَّك لن تزال نجِىَّ هَمّ * تبيت الليل أنت له ضجيع
(Is it in earnest that you will never cease to be the confidant of care, spending the night as its bedfellow?)
And the accusative is permissible in (ليت) by way of the ʿimād, and the nominative for one who says: ليتك قائما. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
ليت الشباب هو الرجيع على الفتى * والشيب كان هو البدئُ الأوّل
(Would that youth were what returns to a young man, and grey hair were the first beginning.)
He used the accusative with (ليت) by way of the ʿimād and the nominative with كان by way of the noun. Definite and indefinite are the same in this.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾: (أَنَّ) came both at its beginning and its end because it is a jazāʾ (conditional), like His saying ﴿كُتِبَ عليه أَنه مَنْ تَولاَّهُ فأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّه﴾ and like His saying ﴿أَلم يَعْلَمُوا أَنه مَنْ يحادِدِ اللَّه ورسولَه فأَنَّ له نارَ جهنَّم﴾. It is permissible in the second (أنّ) to give its alif a kasra, because its dropping is permissible: do you not see that if you said (اعلموا أنّ ما غنمتم من شىء فللّه خمسه) it would be sound? So since its dropping is sound, one gives it a kasra.
His saying: ﴿وَلِذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾: the kinsfolk of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾: the orphans and the poor of the people [at large]; the orphans and the poor of Banū Hāshim are not included in it.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَنتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: al-ʿudwa is the bank of the valley; (الدينا) [i.e. الدنيا, "the nearer"] is the side next to Medina, and (القصوى) ("the farther") the side next to Mecca.
[Translator's note: the source prints «الدينا», apparently a misprint for «الدنيا».]
His saying ﴿وَٱلرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ means Abū Sufyān and the caravan; they were on the seashore.
His saying ﴿أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ is accusative; it means: a place lower than you. Had He described them as being low, meaning "and the caravan were lower", it would have been permissible, in the nominative.
His saying: ﴿وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَيَّ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ﴾: it is written with idghām (assimilation), with a single yāʾ, and that is the reading of most of the readers. Some of them read (حَيىَِ عن بيّنة) with the two made distinct. They assimilated the yāʾ into the yāʾ, though they ought not to have done so, because the second yāʾ is bound to take the fatḥa in faʿala; they assimilated because two vowelled letters of the same kind met. Assimilation is permissible in the dual because of the fixed vowel of the last yāʾ, so you say of two men: قد حَيّا and حَيِيا. In the plural one ought not to assimilate, because its yāʾ would receive the ḍamma while what precedes it has a kasra, so it ought to become quiescent and drop before the wāw of the plural. Yet sometimes the Arabs have used assimilation in the plural, aiming at making the verb forms uniform and having them all doubled.
So they said for حَيِيت: حَيُّوا, and for عيِيت: عَيُّوا. One of them recited to me:
يَحِدن بِنا عن كلّ حَىٍّ كأننا * أخاريس عَيُّوا بالسلام وبالنَّسْبِ
(They [the camels] veer with us away from every tribe, as though we were mutes who could manage neither greeting nor lineage.)
He means النّسَب. Another said:
مِن الذين إذا قلنا: حَدِيثَكم * عَيُّوا، وإن نحن حَدَّثناهُمُ شَغِبَوا
(Of those who, when we say "Your story!", are tongue-tied, and when we talk to them, make an uproar.)
The Arabs are agreed on assimilating التحيّة and التحيّات because of the vowel of the last yāʾ in them, just as they favoured assimilating عىَّ and حَىَّ because of the fixed vowel in them. It may also be correct to assimilate yāʾ into yāʾ in يَحْيا and يَعْيا, though this is rarer than the assimilation in حىّ, because the yāʾ of يحيا is quiescent when it is in the nominative position, so the vowel in it is not fixed. Its justification is that when you put it in the accusative, as in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, ﴿أَليس ذلِك بِقادِرٍ على أَن يُحْيِىَ المَوْتَى﴾, assimilation is correct there; then you make the speech uniform, so that it has assimilation in the nominative and the jussive too; and you say (هو يُحِىُّ ويُمِيت). One of them recited to me:
وكأنها بين النساءِ سبِيكةٌ * تمشى بِسُدَّةِ بَيْتها فَتُعِىُّ
(As if she, among the women, were an ingot [of gold]; she walks to the threshold of her house and grows weary.)
And likewise يَحَيَّان and يَحَيُّون.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَقَالَ لاَ غَالِبَ لَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ﴾: this is Iblīs, who appeared in the form of a man of Banū Kināna called Surāqa ibn Juʿshum. Al-Farrāʾ said: His saying ﴿وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ﴾ means: [your protector] against my people, Banū Kināna, so that they do not interfere with you, and so that they will be with you against Muḥammad ﷺ. When he saw the angels he recognised them, so "he turned back on his heels" (نَكَصَ على عَقِبَيْه). Al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām said to him: "O Surāqa, fleeing without a fight?!" He said: (إنى أَرَى ما لا تَرَوْن) ("I see what you do not see").

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ وَذُوقُواْ﴾ means: "and they say", implied (muḍmar), as He said: ﴿ولَوْ تَرَى إذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهم عِنْدَ رَبِّهِم رَبَّنَا﴾, meaning: they say: (رَبَّنا). And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَإِذْ يرفع إِبراهِيمُ القواعِدَ من البيتِ وإِسماعيلُ﴾ "the two of them saying" ﴿رَبَّنا﴾.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ﴾: (أَنّ) is in the position of the accusative if you make (ذلك) accusative and mean: We did ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ and because ﴿أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾. If you wish, you make (ذلك) in the position of the nominative, and then you make (أنْ) in the position of the nominative, as you say: هذا ذاك ("this is that").

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ means: these denied just as the family of Pharaoh denied, so there befell them what befell the family of Pharaoh.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِم مَّنْ خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ means: if you take them captive, O Muḥammad, then make an example of them to those behind them, those whom you fear will break the covenant: ﴿فَشرِّدْ بِهِمْ﴾.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾: so that they do not break the covenant. It has sometimes been read (مِن خَلْفِهِم), with a kasra on (مِن), but it has no meaning that I approve of in view of the exegesis.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍ خِيَانَةً﴾: He says: breaking of a covenant; ﴿فَٱنْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ with the breaking [i.e. throw back the treaty to them], ﴿عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾: He says: do as they do, equally. It is also said about His saying ﴿عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾: openly, not in secret. His saying ﴿تَخافَنّ﴾ is in the position of the jussive. The Arabs hardly ever put the heavy or the light nūn [of emphasis] in a jazāʾ (conditional) until they join it to (ما); and when they join it, they prefer the nūn. That is because they found that (إمّا), when it is conditional, resembles the (إمّا) of choice ("either… or"), so they introduced the nūn so that the difference between the two might be known by it. Then they made most of its apodoses with fāʾ; thus the Revelation came. He said: ﴿فَإمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِى الحربِ فشَرِّد﴾, and ﴿فإمّا نُرِيَنَّك بعض الذِى نَعِدهم﴾, then He said ﴿فإلينا يرجعون﴾. The fāʾ was chosen because when they put the nūn with (إمّا) they make it the head of the sentence and hardly ever postpone it. It is not their usage to say: اضربه إمّا يقومَنَّ ("Hit him if he stands up"); their usage is to put it first. Since it was bound to come first, it became like something outside the condition, so they favoured the fāʾ with it and preferred it, just as they favoured it in their saying أمّا أخوكم فقاعد ("As for your brother, he is sitting"), since it resembles that.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «فاسحبوا», apparently a misprint for «فاستحبّوا» ("they favoured"); translated in that sense.]

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَبَقُوۤاْ إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ﴾ is with tāʾ (تحسبنّ), there being no disagreement about it. But Ḥamza read it with yāʾ; and we think he took it in light of the reading of ʿAbd Allāh.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا إنهم لا يُعْجِزون). If (أنّهم) is not in it, it is not right for the verb of thinking (ẓann) not to fall on anything [as its object]. Had he meant: "Let not those who disbelieve think that they cannot be frustrated", it would be right, making لا a ṣila (redundant), as in His saying: ﴿وحَرامٌ على قَرْيةٍ أَهلكناها أَنّهم لا يَرْجِعون﴾, meaning: that they will return. And if (أنْ) were with (سبقوا) it would be right, so that you say (ولا يحسب الذين كفروا أن سبقوا).
If someone says: "Is it not Arab usage to say عسيت أذهب ('maybe I shall go') and أريد أقوم معك ('I want to stand with you'), with (أنْ) implied in both? So why is it not permissible to say أظن أقوم ('I think I shall stand') and أظن قمت ('I think I stood')?" I reply: if that were done with ẓanantu when the verb belongs to the one mentioned [i.e. the subject], I would allow it, even if it is a noun, as in their saying: عسى الغُوَيْرُ أَبْؤُساً ("perhaps the little cave holds misfortunes"), the proper form being with أنْ. If you say that, you would say it with aẓunnu too, saying أظن أقوم and أظن قمت, because the verb is yours. But it is not permissible to say أظن يقوم زيد, nor عسيت يقوم زيد, nor أردت يقوم زيد. It is permissible when the verb belongs to him [the subject] because, when you turn yafʿalu into fāʿil (the active participle), it is joined to it and is accusative by its owner; so one says أريد قائما ("I want [to be] standing"), the standing being yours. You do not say أريد قائما زيد; and whoever says this says the like with ẓanantu. One of them recited to me, by Dhū al-Rumma:
أَظَنَّ ابْنُ طُرْثوثِ عُتَيْبةُ ذاهبا * بعادِيَّتِى تَكْذابُه وَجعائِلُهْ
(Did Ibn Ṭurthūth, ʿUtayba, think his lying and his bribes would make off with my wronging?)
So this is a line of reasoning for the reading of Ḥamza: he makes (سبقوا) in the position of the accusative: "Let not those who disbelieve think [themselves] outstripping (sābiqīn)." But I do not like it, because it is anomalous.
[Translator's note: the opening statement that the tāʾ reading has "no disagreement" and then that Ḥamza read with yāʾ is translated as written; it seems to mean that the tāʾ reading is the agreed reading of the majority. The poetic gloss is tentative.]

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُمْ مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ﴾ means the mares. Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to us, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Strength (al-quwwa) is shooting."
His saying: ﴿تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدْوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَآخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ﴾: if you made it [وآخرين] accusative from His saying "and prepare for them, and for others besides them", it would be correct, as in His saying: ﴿والظالمين أَعَدَّ لهم عذابا أليما﴾. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: (ترهبون به عَدُوّاً لِلّهِ وعدوّكم), just as some read in [Sūrat] al-Ṣaff (كونوا أَنْصاراً لِلّهِ).

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن جَنَحُواْ لِلسَّلْمِ فَٱجْنَحْ لَهَا...﴾: if you wish you make (لها) a pronoun referring to al-silm (peace), because it is feminine. If you wish you make it refer to the deed (al-faʿla), as He said ﴿إنّ رَبّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, where only a verb was mentioned before it, so the hāʾ refers to the deed.

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: between the hearts of the Anṣār, of al-Aws and al-Khazraj. There had been war between them, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Medina, Allah set right relations between them through him and through Islam.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «أصح», evidently for «أصلح» ("set right").]

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ﴾: the exegesis came as: Allah suffices you and suffices those who follow you. So the position of the kāf in (حسبك) is genitive (khafḍ), and (مَنْ) is in the position of the accusative according to the exegesis, as the poet said:
إذا كانت الهيجاء وانشقّتِ العصا * فحسبُك والضَّحاكَ سيفٌ مُهَنّد
(When war breaks out and the staff [of unity] is split, an Indian sword suffices you and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.)
It is not frequent in their speech to say حسبك وأخاك until they say حسبك وحسب أخيك; but we allowed it because in (حسبك) there is the sense of a verb acting [on an object], so we referred it back to the meaning of the kāf, not to its form, as in His saying ﴿إنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ﴾, where He referred الأهل back to the meaning of the kāf.
If you wish, you make (مَنْ) in the position of the nominative, and that is the dearer of the two options to me, because the recitation points to the nominative sense; do you not see that He said: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾: the Prophet ﷺ used to send his Companions on campaigns on the basis that ten were for a hundred and one for ten, and so they were. Then it became hard for them that one should be matched against ten, so there was revealed: ﴿ٱلآنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوۤاْ أَلْفَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلآنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوۤاْ أَلْفَيْنِ﴾: so Allah made clear their strength first and last. Al-Kisāʾī held this view and put (من) in the nominative.
[Translator's note: the last sentence appears to belong to the discussion of ﴿وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ﴾ in verse 64; it is translated where the source places it.]

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَىٰ﴾: its meaning is: it was not proper for him on the day of Badr to accept ransom for the captives ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُثْخِنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: until he prevails over many of those on the earth. Then there was revealed His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾: concerning the ransom of the captives and the spoils. It has also been read (أَُسارى), and each is correct. And His saying (أَن يَّكُونَ) [is read] with the masculine and the feminine [يكون / تكون], like His saying (يَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتهُم) and (تَشْهَدُ).

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, then He said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ﴾: in inheritance. They used to inherit from one another to the exclusion of their relatives who had not emigrated.
That is His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُواْ مَا لَكُمْ مِّن وَلاَيَتِهِم﴾, meaning: of their inheritances.
Putting a kasra on the wāw in al-wilāya is more pleasing to me than a fatḥa, because it is mostly given a fatḥa when it has the meaning of support (nuṣra). Al-Kisāʾī used to read it with a fatḥa, taking it to mean support, and I do not think he knew the exegesis. For walītuhu wilāyatan (I took charge of it) they choose the kasra; but we have heard both, with fatḥa and kasra, in both their meanings. The poet said:
دعِيهمْ فَهُمْ أَلْبٌ عَلَىَّ وِلايةٌ * وحَفْرُهُمُ أَنْ يَعْلَموا ذاكَ دائب
(Leave them, for they are banded together against me in alliance, and their digging to find that out is unceasing.)
Then there was revealed afterwards: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ مَعَكُمْ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مِنكُمْ وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾: if you do not inherit from one another on the basis of kinship, there will be discord. It is also mentioned that it concerns support: if you do not support one another, there will be discord.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ مَعَكُمْ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مِنكُمْ وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾: so they inherited from one another, and this latter verse abrogated the verse before it. That is that His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾.
[Translator's note: the last sentence breaks off in the source; translated as it stands.]

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَنْفَالِ﴾: it was revealed concerning the spoils (anfāl) of the people of Badr. That is because when the Prophet ﷺ saw how few the people were and their dislike of fighting, he said: "Whoever kills a man shall have such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive shall have such-and-such."
When he had finished with the people of Badr, Saʿd ibn Muʿādh stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you give these what you named for them, many of the Muslims will remain with nothing." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿قُلِ ٱلأَنفَالُ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾: he does with them what he wills. So they fell silent, with some dislike of that in their hearts.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾: this hāʾ is for the reinforcing (al-irdāf): Allah did not make the reinforcing ﴿إِلاَّ بُشْرَىٰ﴾.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِّنْهُ﴾: the Muslims spent the night of Badr without water, and they awoke in a state of major ritual impurity (janāba). Satan whispered to them, saying: "You claim that you are on the religion of Allah, yet you are without water while your enemy is at the water, and you pray in a state of janāba!" So Allah sent the sky upon them, and they drank and washed; and Allah removed from them the defilement (rijz) of Satan, meaning his whispering. They were in sand in which the feet sank, and the rain made it firm until men could tread firmly on it. That is His saying: ﴿وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلأَقْدَامَ﴾.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾: an angel would come to a man among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ and say: "I heard these people — meaning Abū Sufyān and his companions — saying: By Allah, if they charge at us, we shall be routed." Then the Muslims would tell one another of that, and their spirits would be strengthened. That is His inspiring the angels.
His saying: ﴿فَٱضْرِبُواْ فَوْقَ ٱلأَعْنَاقِ﴾: He taught them the places to strike, and said: strike the heads, the hands and the feet.
That is His saying: ﴿وَٱضْرِبُواْ مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ﴾.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾: He addressed the polytheists.
Then He said: ﴿وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾: (أَنّ) is accusative from two directions.
As for one of them: that is "because (بأن) the disbelievers have the punishment of the Fire"; the bāʾ was dropped and so it became accusative. The other accusative is that you imply a verb, as in the saying of the poet:
تسمع للأحشاء منه لغطا * ولليدين جُسْأَةً وبَدَدَا
(You hear a clamour from his insides, and [see] in his two forelegs stiffness and a wide stance.)
He implied (and you see in the two forelegs). Likewise He said ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾, and know ﴿َأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾. And if you wish you may make (أن) in the position of the nominative, meaning: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾, and that is ﴿أَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾. Similar to it in the Book of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿خَتَمَ اللّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةً﴾: ʿĀṣim read it so, according to what al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to me; and he claimed that ʿĀṣim took it from him twice with the accusative [Translator's note: the source has "بانصب", a misprint for بالنصب]. And likewise His saying: ﴿وحُورٌ عِينٌ﴾.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مُتَحَرِّفاً لِّقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ﴾: it is an exception, and the one withdrawing (المُتَحَيِّز) is other than مَن. And if you wish you may make it part of the description of مَن, and it is on the pattern of your saying: "except that he turns his back on them", meaning to return to the attack; as you say in speech: "عبدالله يأتيك إلاّ ماشيا" ("ʿAbd Allāh will come to you, unless on foot") and "يأتيك إلا أن تمنعه الرحلة" ("he will come to you unless the journey prevents him"). And (إلا) here does not have the sense of His saying ﴿إلى طعام غيرَ ناظرين إنَاهُ﴾, because (غير) [there] follows the pattern of (لا), not the pattern of (إلا).

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمَآ أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ despite their reluctance: so proceed with Allah's command concerning the spoils as you proceeded with your setting out while they were reluctant.
And it is said about it: they ask you about the spoils just as they disputed with you on the day of Badr and said: "You brought us out for booty and did not tell us of fighting so that we might prepare for it." That is His saying: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾

farraa:6-7.t:
His saying: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾; and His saying: ﴿فاتَّقُوا الله وَأَصْلِحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾: He commanded the Muslims to share with one another in the spoils after they had been granted to them, as a command that is not obligatory.
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحْدَى ٱلطَّائِفَتِيْنِ﴾, then He said ﴿أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ﴾: He put (إحدى الطائفتين) in the accusative by "يعد", then repeated it, on the sense of: He promises you that one of the two parties is yours; as He said: ﴿فهل ينظرون إِلا الساعة﴾, then said: ﴿أَن تَأْتِيهم بغتة﴾: أن is in the position of the accusative just as الساعة was put in the accusative. And His saying: ﴿ولولا رِجال مؤمِنون ونِساء مؤمِنات﴾: He put them in the nominative by "لولا", then said: ﴿أَن تطئوهم﴾, so أن is in the position of the nominative by "لولا".

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿ بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾, and it is read (مُرْدَفين). As for (مردِفين), it means following one another; and (مردَفين): it was done to them [i.e. they were made to follow].
